blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights Google Vizier as a scalable internal service for black-box optimization, emphasizing its role in optimizing complex systems where understanding is infeasible. He notes the paper's opening insight—that modern systems are so complex they're effectively black boxes—and praises Vizier's versatility, from optimizing Google's cookie recipes to tuning machine learning hyperparameters and A/B testing web properties. Colyer appreciates the service's simplicity in design, its support for multiple optimization algorithms (defaulting to Batched Gaussian Process Bandits), and its ability to handle early stopping and transfer learning. The blog post also underscores Vizier's integration into Google's infrastructure, including its use in HyperTune and massive-scale studies affecting over a billion users.
paper_title: Google Vizier: A Service for Black-Box Optimization
